title: Who gets punished?
hook: Could punishment harm cooperation if high contributors are targeted?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish punishment of free riders from punishment of cooperators.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish punishment of free riders from punishment of cooperators.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: In a toy public-goods ledger, someone starts with twenty, contributes ten and receives a penalty of three. What remains in that private account? Toy inputs A=[20, 10, 3]; B=[20, 0, 3].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[7, 10, 3], [17, 0, 3]]. Labels: Remaining, Contributed, Penalty.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The same penalty can target a contributor or a non-contributor. Their private balances make the distinction visible. Counting punishment alone therefore loses information about who was punished and what behavior it discourages.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Endowment=20, Contribution=0, Punishment=3. What is Remaining? Answer: 17.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Endowment=20, Contribution=0, Punishment=3. What is Remaining?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 17. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: In some cities, players punish the cooperators, not just free riders, which wrecks cooperation (Herrmann, Thöni & Gächter, 2008).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish punishment of free riders from punishment of cooperators.
